title: Am I an Israelite Indeed
description: Am I an Israelite Indeed in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 502 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For Inward Truth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Am I an Is-rae-lite in-deed. With-out a false dis-guise? Have I re-nounced my sins, and left My re-fu-ges of lies?

lines: Have I renounced my sins, and left
Say, does my heart unchanged remain,
What is the rule by which I walk,
Cause me, O God of truth and grace,
If I am wrong, O set me right!

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
